哈丁格小提琴主要見於挪威西南部，用於舞蹈伴奏，常伴隨節奏強烈的跺腳聲；也曾在婚禮: The Hardanger fiddle is found mainly in south-western Norway, where it accompanies dancing, often with a strong rhythmic stamping of the feet; it also once led wedding processions to the church door. Edvard Grieg arranged Hardanger folk tunes and wrote a Hardanger fiddle part for the first Peer Gynt suite by Ibsen, whose "Morning Mood" opens with a phrase taken from the instrument's sympathetic-string tuning. On recordings it can be heard with an old church organ, as in "Rosa i Botnen"; it also appears in solo and string-quartet settings.
哈丁格小提琴最早實例為1651年Ole Jonsen Jaastad在挪威哈丁格: The earliest surviving example of the Hardanger fiddle was made in 1651 by Ole Jonsen Jaastad in Hardanger, Norway, and the old body was rounder and narrower; after about 1850 it changed to the modern form, close to the violin. It is found mainly in south-western Norway, and its relation with the Christian church has been complicated: during the 19th-century religious revival it was burned or hidden, and only in the 20th century did Johannes Dahle, Gjermund Haugen and others play it in church. Edvard Grieg brought its folk tunes into the first Peer Gynt suite, and in recent years it has been taken up by Japanese musicians and international composers.
哈丁格小提琴琴身採用優質木材製造，通常琴板採用雲杉或松木，背板與側板則選用楓木或: The body of the Hardanger fiddle is made of good timber, usually a top of spruce or pine and a back and sides of maple or birch. The neck and the head are mostly carved from maple. The strings were traditionally gut, and today steel or nylon strings are also used. The bow stick is of Brazilwood, with horsehair for the hair. The bridge and the pegs are mostly of blackwood or ebony. The surface is usually given a natural oil or varnish, which keeps the warm, old look.
哈丁格小提琴音色獨特而迷人，具有明亮卻不刺耳的質感，帶有溫潤的民謠氣息。由於擁有: The Hardanger fiddle has a distinctive, attractive tone: bright without being harsh, with a warm folk character. Because it has eight or nine strings, four of them played and the rest sympathetic, it produces rich overtones and natural resonance. The sympathetic strings sound of themselves when the played strings vibrate, which gives the instrument a particular metallic sheen and a lingering tail of sound. Its range covers the usual range of the violin, but the tone has more of a national character. Against the standard violin the Hardanger is warmer and fuller, with a slight quiver; beside the guitar it is brighter and clearer. These qualities make it especially suited to Norwegian folk music, and it gives off a strong northern atmosphere.

哈當厄小提琴又稱挪威小提琴，是挪威傳統弦鳴樂器，分類編號321.322-71。它: The Hardanger fiddle, also called the Norwegian fiddle, is a traditional Norwegian chordophone, classification number 321.322-71. It looks much like a violin, with a thinner top and usually eight or nine strings; four are played with the bow as on a violin, and the rest, the understrings or sympathetic strings, resonate when the played strings sound. The bowing is lighter and more bouncing, and two of the upper strings are often played together to produce double stops. In south-western Norway it is much used for dancing and is also connected with church occasions, traditionally leading the bride's procession to the church door.

The left hand stops the strings, or changes their sounding length, to set the pitch, and the right hand sets them vibrating to make the sound. A chordophone sounds because the vibration of the strings is amplified by the soundbox. Bow evenly, using the weight of the arm rather than the strength of the wrist.
